To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a) a 1D model of a gear pair, based on a 3D FE simulation of the meshed gears, can be created; b) the model can be used for predicting gear dynamics in a wide range of operating conditions.

a new numerical method has been proposed, based on pre-strain modal analysis and 1D model, to estimate the dynamic transmission error of a pair of gears in steady-state condition; the proposed method has been applied to a pair of spur gears and results are compared with those obtained by a 3D model.

the proposed approach allows to efficiently simulate the non-linear dynamic behaviour of gear transmissions, with the advantage of being based on a 1D model, which can be used in a variety of different applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a numerical procedure to estimate the dynamic properties of a 3D FE gear model, which can be used to calibrate an equivalent 1D gear model.

developing a methodology to efficiently simulate the dynamics of gear transmissions, which is able to combine the advantages of 3D modelling with those of 1D modelling, in terms of computational requirements and accuracy.
the development of a methodology for the efficient numerical analysis of non-linear gear dynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach can be used to efficiently simulate the non-linear gear dynamics, with a computational cost much lower than a 3D FE simulation.
the proposed method allows for an efficient and reliable estimation of the dynamic TE of 1D models, with a limited computational effort.
the proposed methodology allows to efficiently and accurately estimate the dynamic TE for a gear pair under steady state conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed methodology can be considered a useful tool for the preliminary design of gear transmissions, in order to identify the most suitable gear pair geometry and to assess the dynamic behaviour of the system.

the proposed approach can be successfully used to estimate the 1D dynamic properties of a gear pair from the 3D model, with a limited computational effort.
the proposed method allows to efficiently simulate the dynamic behavior of a gear pair in steady-state conditions, by combining the advantages of 3D FE simulations and of 1D analytical models.
